candidates.name: LIDAR Composite DTM 2017 - 25cm
verified_facts: The 25cm composite is retired and was replaced by the 1m composite.
It merged and re-sampled time-stamped archive surveys and used the newest/best-resolution repeat survey.
It used 5km ASCII grids, Ordnance Datum Newlyn and OSTN15, with survey-index files identifying contributing surveys.
semantic_limits: Historical high resolution does not make a retired composite a current primary source; it is lineage evidence only.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Surface Model (DSM) - 2m
verified_facts: The 2m DSM includes surface objects such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
The 2022 composite merges time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys and uses bilinear interpolation where data is resampled.
Metadata index catalogues identify which survey was used at a location.
semantic_limits: DSM values are not substituted for the bare-earth DTM parcel result.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite First Return Digital Surface Model (FZ_DSM) - 2m
verified_facts: The 2m first-return DSM includes objects above the terrain surface.
It is derived from National LIDAR Programme capture and merges surveys using feathering along overlaps.
Metadata index catalogues identify contributing surveys by location.
semantic_limits: Feathered first-return surface data is diagnostic only and is excluded from bare-earth height-difference measurement.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 10m
verified_facts: The 10m DTM is resampled from the 2m composite DTM using bilinear interpolation.
It remains a bare-earth terrain product but at substantially coarser spatial resolution.
semantic_limits: The 10m product is a coarse sanity check only and cannot replace the 1m primary parcel sample.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 grid data technical specification
verified_facts: Each 5m grid value is calculated as a mean of heights across the whole 5m pixel.
ASCII z values are positioned at the pixel centre, 2.5m from the tile corner offset.
A 5km tile contains 1000 by 1000 pixels and values are stored to the nearest 0.01m.
semantic_limits: Stored 0.01m precision and pixel-centre coordinates do not imply centimetric vertical accuracy.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 source data
verified_facts: Source TIN z values have geographic-class positional accuracy requirements.
Absolute height accuracy is assessed using RMSE against true elevation.
Terrain modelling includes smoothness/geometric-fidelity constraints and no single point should exceed the stated 99% confidence level.
semantic_limits: Source modelling and geographic-class RMSE remain secondary to the EA 1m primary source for this slot.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 5 product documentation
verified_facts: OS Terrain 5 is a 5m DTM supplied as grid and contour data.
The product is updated quarterly in January, April, July and October.
OS describes typical product accuracy as greater than 2m RMSE and supplies 5km tiles.
semantic_limits: Quarterly publication cadence and product-level accuracy are not parcel acquisition dates or sub-metre validation.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 overview
verified_facts: OS Terrain 50 is a lower-resolution DTM intended for broad-area analysis.
Its grid has been verified to 4m RMSE.
semantic_limits: Terrain 50 is too coarse for parcel extrema and is retained only as a broad sanity/source-family check.

candidates.name: Practice guide 40 supplement 1 - basis of HM Land Registry plans
verified_facts: Ordnance Survey mapping is multi-purpose topographic mapping and is not intended to represent property boundaries.
HMLR title plans use different map scales depending on context, commonly 1:1250 urban and 1:2500 rural.
semantic_limits: OS topographic linework and map scale must not be converted into an exact cadastral parcel boundary.

candidates.name: Preparing plans for HM Land Registry applications (PG40s2)
verified_facts: The supplement is for preparing deed plans and was updated 13 October 2025.
Plans for searches of part are considered using the same guidelines as transfers or leases of part.
semantic_limits: Application-plan acceptability establishes identifiability for registration workflow, not centimetric legal-boundary or terrain accuracy.

candidates.name: Practice guide 40 supplement 5 - title plan detailed guidance
verified_facts: The title plan must be read with the register and filed documents.
Adjoining title plans can be based on different versions of Ordnance Survey mapping.
Title plans identify general extent and show general boundaries unless a boundary is determined.
semantic_limits: Title-plan version, red edging, dimensions and scale are legal/registration evidence, not exact terrain-sampling geometry by themselves.

candidates.name: HM Land Registry plans guidance hub
verified_facts: HMLR routes users to separate plan guides for map basis, application plans, boundaries, determined boundaries, title plans and estate surveying.
semantic_limits: Guide routing establishes the correct authority chain; it does not itself supply parcel geometry or elevation.

candidates.name: Developing estates plan requirements and surveying specification (PG41s5)
verified_facts: Estate plans must be based on an accurate survey and drawn at a stated scale.
The guide supplies plottable plan tolerances tied to map scale and measured distance.
Survey control should remain on the datum used for the original survey.
semantic_limits: Registration-plan survey tolerances are horizontal plan-production tolerances and are not LiDAR vertical RMSE or exact legal-boundary guarantees.

candidates.name: Joint statement: Ordnance Survey and Land Registry
verified_facts: HMLR title plans use red lines for registered extent and dotted lines where a boundary is not defined by an OS physical feature.
Ownership of individual boundary structures is usually not shown by the registered title.
semantic_limits: Mapped physical features are contextual evidence and cannot be assumed to be the exact legal boundary.

candidates.name: WCS 2.1 Core normative document
verified_facts: WCS 2.1 specifies access to multidimensional coverage data and supports CIS 1.1.
WCS 2.0 service extensions remain applicable under WCS 2.1 subject to compatibility updates.
semantic_limits: WCS conformance identifies service semantics; it does not establish the accuracy or provenance of a particular EA elevation value.

candidates.name: WCS Interpolation Extension 1.0
verified_facts: The extension controls interpolation during GetCoverage processing.
Interpolation affects operations such as scaling and CRS change.
Supported methods are advertised by the service; an interpolation parameter has effect only when an operation actually involves interpolation.
semantic_limits: Interpolation must be explicit in reproducibility evidence and must not be silently treated as a native measurement.

candidates.name: Coverage Implementation Schema 1.1 normative document
verified_facts: CIS defines domainSet, rangeSet, rangeType and metadata for interoperable coverages.
Each direct position must have exactly one range value, with null values used where values are unknown.
RangeType may restrict meaningful interpolation methods.
semantic_limits: Coverage structural conformance does not prove terrain-source authority or vertical accuracy.

candidates.name: Abstract Specification Topic 6 Part 1: Fundamentals
verified_facts: Topic 6 Part 1 is an approved OGC Abstract Specification for coverage geometry and functions.
It provides the conceptual coverage model used by downstream implementation standards.
semantic_limits: An abstract coverage model defines semantics, not parcel-specific elevation provenance or accuracy.

candidates.name: CF-netCDF 3.0 encoding using GML Coverage Application Schema
verified_facts: The standard defines encoding and exchange of multidimensional gridded and multi-point coverage data.
It distinguishes coverage model, data format and protocol characteristics.
semantic_limits: Encoding a coverage as CF-netCDF changes representation/interchange, not the underlying numeric accuracy.

candidates.name: WCS 2.0 Earth Observation Application Profile
verified_facts: The profile normatively depends on range subsetting, scaling, interpolation and CRS-related WCS extensions.
It separates these processing capabilities into distinct conformance dependencies.
semantic_limits: Profile conformance and processing capability do not independently validate a parcel elevation measurement.
